 Warren Buffett takes another step toward giving away his entire fortune
 The billionaire investor converted 6,150 Class A Berkshire Hathaway shares into 9.225 million Class B shares for four foundations run by his family

 By Louis Casiano FOXBusiness Warren Buffett, donated roughly $5.5 billion of Berkshire Hathaway stock to four foundations, according to his annual Thanksgiving letter.  ( Houston Cofield/Bloomberg via Getty Images ) 
 Warren Buffett has donated roughly $5.5 billion worth of Berkshire Hathaway stock to four philanthropic foundations as part of his annual Thanksgiving gift, the legendary investor announced in a Monday letter.
 The 96-year-old converted 6,150 Class A shares into 9,225,000 Class B shares, donating 3,690,000 shares to The Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation, named after his late first wife, and 1,845,000 shares each to The Sherwood Foundation, The Howard G. Buffett Foundation, and the NoVo Foundation.
 The latter three foundations are led by Buffett’s children: Susie, Howard and Peter Buffett. Buffett has previously said he plans to give away his entire fortune.
 WARREN BUFFETT PENS LAST LETTER AS ABEL PREPARES TO TAKE OVER 
 "Today’s gift is consistent with the plan I have previously described," Buffett wrote. "All my Berkshire shares will be donated to the four foundations, with the goal of growing the grants each year. Reaching this goal will largely depend on stock market conditions between now and the target date. My children have given thoughtfully to worthy causes for decades, and I trust 100% both their abilities and their fidelity."

 In his brief letter, Buffett reflected on the enduring value of generosity , writing that kindness "compounds" at a better rate than "anything Charlie and I ever bought."

 Charlie Munger, the longtime vice chairman of Berkshire Hathaway, died in November 2023.

 "Both of us received beyond measurement costless benefits from a few teachers such as Ben Graham, Joe Rosenfield and Tom Murphy," Buffett wrote. "Because of this we not only prospered mightily but were able to pass along many of the benefits we received."
 "Much of my good fortune has come in the form of people who were kind to me and expected nothing in return. I’m grateful to every one of them," he added. "This Thanksgiving, thank one of those selfless people in your own life. Better yet, be a benefactor for someone else."
 The Sherwood, Howard G. Buffett and NoVo foundations are heavily funded by Berkshire Hathaway stock donations .
